Name: Fashion Equipment
Author: slpOff
Description:
[b]description[/b]

Collect, wear, and display your Fashion Sense outfits as physical items. Fashion Equipment automatically registers hats, shirts, pants, shoes, hairstyles, and accessories from your installed packs, adds slots for layering accessories, and offers five clothing rack styles. Buy outfits, find random clothing drops, customize colors, dress mannequins, and complete a shirt collection with optional Perfection integration.

[b]Installation[/b]

Requires [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.14 or later[/b], [b]SMAPI 4.0 or later[/b], and [b]Fashion Sense 7.5.0 or later[/b]. Install the Fashion Sense content packs you want to use separately; clothing packs are not included.

[list=1]
[*]Close the game and SMAPI.
[/*]
[*]Extract the download and place the
[code]FashionEquipment[/code]folder inside your game's
[code]Mods[/code]folder.
[/*]
[*]Install Fashion Sense and your chosen content packs, then launch the game through SMAPI.
[/*]
[/list]Content pack files do not need to be edited. Install [b]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/b] to change settings in the game.

[b]Getting clothing[/b]

The mod automatically finds available hats, shirts, pants, shoes, hairstyles, and accessories in your installed Fashion Sense packs and registers them as items. Locked appearances, bodies, and sleeves are excluded.

Each player can buy one of each item per day. Reopening the shop or reloading your save does not change that day's selection. Stock refreshes the next day. If your installed packs contain fewer items than the quota, the shop offers only those available. Existing shop merchandise is preserved.

Enable [b]Hat Mouse sells all items[/b] in GMCM to offer the entire catalogue of hats, accessories, and hairstyles at once. Prices and per-item daily purchase limits stay the same. Save your settings and reopen the shop to apply the change.

[b]Random drops[/b]

[list]
[*]Breaking a stone in the Mines or Skull Cavern has a default [b]0.2%[/b] chance to drop one extra clothing item.
[/*]
[*]Felling a mature ordinary tree has a default [b]1%[/b] chance to drop one extra clothing item. Shaking trees, removing stumps or saplings, and cutting fruit trees do not count.
[/*]
[*]Hats, shirts, pants, shoes, and accessories can drop. [b]Hairstyles are sold in shops and never drop randomly.[/b]
[/*]
[/list]Adjust each drop chance from 0% to 100% in GMCM. Set it to 0% to disable drops, or 100% to guarantee a drop for each qualifying action.

[b]Wearing clothing and accessories[/b]

Equip hats, shirts, pants, and shoes in the inventory's standard equipment slots. Use the panel to the left of your inventory for accessories, extra hats, and hairstyles.

[list]
[*]Pick up an item and click the [b]+ slot[/b] to equip one item. A new equipped slot appears above it, while the + slot stays empty.
[/*]
[*]Both vanilla hats and Fashion Sense hats are supported, and multiple hats can be layered.
[/*]
[*]Placing a hairstyle in the + slot equips it in a fixed hair slot below the accessories. Only one hairstyle can be equipped at a time.
[/*]
[*]Briefly click an equipped slot with an empty cursor to pick up and unequip its item. Place a single replacement item into the slot to swap it.
[/*]
[*]Scroll over the panel with the mouse wheel when the list grows too long. The hair and + slots remain visible.
[/*]
[/list]Hair is drawn first, followed by accessories from the top slot downward. Accessories in lower slots appear in front of those above them. Shirts, pants, and shoes cannot be equipped in this panel.

For controllers, enable the game's menu snapping option. Press left from the leftmost inventory slot to enter the panel. Use [b]up/down[/b] to select, [b]A[/b] to equip or unequip, [b]X[/b] to change color, and [b]B or right[/b] to return.

[b]Dyeing equipped clothing[/b]

With an empty cursor, [b]hold left-click on an equipped clothing slot for about 0.5 seconds[/b] to open the vanilla color picker. This works with standard equipment slots and accessory and hair slots.

Adjust hue, saturation, and brightness to preview the result on your character facing forward. Choose [b]Apply or press Enter[/b] to save. Choose [b]Cancel, press Esc, or close the window[/b] to restore the original color. With a controller, use up/down to select a slider, left/right to adjust, A to apply, and B to cancel.

Supported appearances include Fashion Sense outfits that allow dyeing and dyeable vanilla clothing. Fixed-color and prismatic appearances cannot be recolored.

Buy racks from [b]Robin's shop[/b]. Racks cannot be crafted.

[list=1]
[*]Place the rack like ordinary furniture. Wall-mounted racks go on indoor walls; other styles can be placed on indoor or outdoor floors.
[/*]
[*]Select a clothing item and [b]right-click[/b] the part of the rack where you want to hang it.
[/*]
[*]Choose a hanger color with the vanilla color picker, then select [b]Hang[/b]. One garment is placed on the nearest available hanger. This color affects the small hanger, separately from the garment's dye.

[/*]

[/list]Removing a garment from the middle does not move the others. When garments overlap, clicking selects the one displayed in front. Hanger colors are saved for each garment.

Disable [b]Enable clothing sway[/b] in GMCM to keep hanging clothes and their click areas stationary. Adjust [b]Hanging clothing size[/b] from 100% to 300% to enlarge the display. Larger garments may overlap.

[b]Dressing mannequins[/b]

Hold a clothing item and [b]right-click[/b] a mannequin to equip it. Hats and accessories can be layered, while hairstyles replace one another.

Select an empty inventory slot and [b]left-click[/b] the relevant body area to retrieve its equipment into your inventory.

[table][tr][th]Click area[/th]

Stacked headwear is removed last-added first. Clicking an empty area does not remove equipment from another area. If your inventory is full, the equipment stays on the mannequin.

[b]Shift + empty-hand right-click[/b], or using a [b]pickaxe or axe[/b], drops the most recently added extra headwear at your feet. Replacing a hairstyle also returns the previous hairstyle at your feet. An appearance copied with a Hand Mirror does not store a physical item, so it cannot be retrieved as an item by left-clicking.

[b]Shirt collection and Perfection[/b]

A [b]shirt collection tab with a Cloth icon[/b] appears below the existing tabs on the left of the Collections menu. Obtaining physical shirts, including vanilla and Fashion Sense shirts, records them automatically.

[list]
[*]Different colors and quality levels of the same shirt count as one type.
[/*]
[*]Selling or discarding a shirt does not remove its collection record.
[/*]
[*]Shirts already in your inventory or equipped in an existing save are recorded too. Take shirts out of chests or racks into your inventory to register them.
[/*]
[*]Collected shirts show their icons; missing shirts appear as silhouettes. Use the arrows at the bottom to change pages.
[/*]
[*]Hats, pants, shoes, hairstyles, and accessories do not count toward the shirt collection.
[/*]
[/list]By default, shirt collection is included in [b]Perfection requirements[/b] and appears on the tracker in Qi's Walnut Room. If Perfection Handbook is installed, it also shows your progress there.

Disable [b]Include shirts in perfection[/b] in GMCM to exclude shirts from the Perfection calculation while keeping the collection tab and records. Save your settings and reopen the tracker or handbook. In multiplayer, the host's setting applies, and the farm uses the highest shirt collection percentage achieved by a single player.

[b]Frequently asked questions[/b]

[b]I installed a clothing pack, but its items are missing.[/b]

Check that Fashion Sense loaded the pack successfully. Restart the game, or run
[code]fe_reload[/code]in the SMAPI console if you refreshed packs during the session.

[b]How can I find a specific outfit directly?[/b]

Use
[code]fe_list search text[/code]in the SMAPI console to search by name or category. Run the
[code]fe_give[/code]command shown in the results to receive one item. You need room in your inventory.

[b]Can I remove a pack after storing its clothing?[/b]

Keep the packs required by items you wear or store installed. Missing packs prevent their appearances from displaying or their items from being used. Renaming a pack or appearance may also affect existing items.
